transcript.text: Thanks everyone for being here. As you know, the customer-notification service needs a production message-streaming platform before its next integration milestone, and we've narrowed it down to two finalists: KafkaCloud and StreamGrid. Both passed our benchmark of 20,000 messages per second with sub-250-millisecond median delivery latency. The draft architecture currently recommends StreamGrid based on simpler operational setup and an initial capacity estimate of four brokers. Before I make a final decision, I'd like to go through sign-off from each of your areas -- backend, support engineering, security, and FinOps. Could each of you share your assessment of the two platforms, starting with any concerns or considerations from your perspective?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag something important before we go further. While testing the notification client's retry behavior this morning, I confirmed that the service already has a KafkaCloud-compatible producer and consumer path. This means using KafkaCloud would only require about two days of adapter cleanup, whereas moving to StreamGrid would require a new two-week client integration. I haven't updated the architecture document with this yet, but it directly affects the StreamGrid recommendation -- the simpler operational setup comes with a significantly longer integration timeline that wasn't reflected in the draft.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to share something critical from a customer escalation yesterday. I confirmed that three enterprise customers require notifications for each account to remain in order. KafkaCloud can guarantee that ordering using a customer_id partition key, but StreamGrid's tested mode cannot. I have not yet added this requirement to the review ticket, which I realize I should have done earlier.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to raise a security concern that changes the picture. During a data-flow review this afternoon, I confirmed that notification payloads contain phone numbers, which means they must be stored and processed in eu-central-1. KafkaCloud offers that processing region for this service, but StreamGrid's selected tier does not. I have not yet filed the security architecture note on this, but this is a hard compliance requirement -- StreamGrid's current tier cannot meet our data residency obligations for this workload.

transcript.text: I need to share something from the FinOps side that I found this morning when I reconciled the cloud account. We already have existing KafkaCloud reserved-capacity credits that cover exactly six production brokers through the service's first year. StreamGrid has no equivalent credit. This means a KafkaCloud production deployment would provision all six brokers -- setting production_broker_count to exactly 6 to use the full reserved-capacity allocation -- at no additional cost for the first year. I should note that I have not yet amended the four-broker estimate in the draft architecture, so that figure doesn't reflect this reserved-capacity allocation.
transcript.speaker: A5

commitments.detail: Update the draft architecture to reflect KafkaCloud as the selected platform, replacing the StreamGrid recommendation.
Revise the broker count estimate from four to six to reflect the reserved-capacity allocation.
Add the per-account notification ordering requirement and the customer_id partition key guarantee to the review ticket.
File the security architecture note documenting that notification payloads contain phone numbers and require eu-central-1 processing.
Proceed with the approximately two-day KafkaCloud adapter cleanup for the existing producer and consumer path.
